items.title: Alliance Air pays over ₹16 lakh to 33 passengers after consumer court issues NBW over flight cancellation
items.summary: Over two years after abruptly cancelling a Hyderabad–Mysore flight, Alliance Air has cleared more than ₹16 lakh in compensation to 33 passengers following the issuance of non-bailable warrants by a Hyderabad consumer commission [Radha Devi Mandhana vs M/s The Alliance Aviation Ltd]. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-II, Hyderabad, comprising President Vakkanti Narasimha Rao and Members P V T R Jawahar Babu and Suma Vala , terminated execution proceedings on October 14 after recording satisfaction of the decree. The Bench also recalled the non-bailable warrants (NBWs) previously issued against airline officials. The dispute arose from an incident on June 2, 2022, when a 33-member family group, including senior citizens and infants, arrived at Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Airport to board a flight to Mysore. Less than three hours before departure, the airline sent an SMS notifying them of the flight's cancellation. Left stranded without assistance or refreshments, the passengers were offered alternate seats only for a few members of the group, which they could not take. items.title: Children too have fundamental right to access internet; can't deny it citing online harm: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court has held that children have a fundamental right to access and use the internet and protecting them from online harm cannot justify denying them access altogether [Just Rights for Children Alliance & Anr. v. S. Harish & Ors.]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran passed the order while issuing extensive directions to detect and remove child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) online. The Court said that internet access, as a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution, is available to children as well as adults. “We have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. Our children, irrespective of their age enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing. items.title: Delhi High Court says no need to disclose records of foreign travel in IAF aircraft by PM, ex-PM
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has set aside a Central Information Commission (CIC) order directing Indian Air Force to disclose detailed records relating to Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi and former PM Manmohan Singh’s foreign travel under the Right to Information Act (RTI Act). Justice Amit Mahajan noted that the RTI applicant, retired Commodore Lokesh Batra, had sought details about Special Flight Returns (SFR) Part I & Part II, which include details of aircraft, aircrew, the entire entourage, including names of all the Special Protection Group (SPG) personnel travelling with the PM. The Court observed that providing this information could compromise national security and endanger the PM's life and physical safety. “The potential implications of such disclosure for national security and the security apparatus accompanying the Hon’ble Prime Minister cannot be disregarded,” the High Court said in its October 15 order. items.title: CJI Surya Kant inaugurates J&K High Court's Ladakh bench in Leh
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Sunday inaugurated Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court's newly constituted Ladakh bench in Leh. Supreme Court Justices MM Sundresh , PS Narasimha and Arun Palli , along with judges of the High Court, were also present on the occasion. Attorney General for India R Venkatramani and Ladakh Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena also attended the event. Ladakh bench inauguration - Group photo Hearing of cases at the Ladakh bench will commence from October 21. A division bench of Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Sanjay Parihar is expected to take up five cases on Wednesday. Justice Parihar will also preside over a single bench and hear cases on Thursday and Friday as well. The High Court has identified a total of 75 cases for listing before the bench situated in Leh. The Union government had approved the establishment of the Ladakh bench for the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh in August this year. Following the decision, the High Court on October 5 selected Leh as the place for holding sittings of the High Court in the Union Territory of Ladakh.
